proposal.utterance: Classify 'a property status' in BFO terms.

entities.label: PropertyStatus
entities.rationale: A property status (e.g., owned, mortgaged, encumbered, in trust) is a determinate, measurable property that inheres in exactly one bearer — the material entity (land parcel, building, chattel) or the legal person to whom the status is attributed. It is not externally grounded by a social role assignment in the way BFO Role is (though see open_questions), nor is it a capacity or tendency (Disposition). Quality is the most natural fit: it is a specifically dependent continuant that characterises its bearer at a time and can change (e.g., from 'unencumbered' to 'mortgaged') without the bearer ceasing to exist.

relations.rationale: PropertyStatus is a subclass of BFO Quality: it is a specifically dependent continuant inhering in a bearer (a piece of property or a legal person) and characterising it at a time.

open_questions: Should 'property status' be understood as a legal/institutional status (e.g., 'fee simple owner', 'lessee') rather than a simple quality? If so, BFO Role (BFO_0000023) — externally grounded by social/legal recognition — might be preferable or a parallel class (PropertyStatusRole) may be needed alongside PropertyStatus as Quality.
Is 'property' here real property (land/buildings), personal property (chattels), or intellectual property? The bearer of the quality differs in each case and may affect the modelling.

Is a specific property status (e.g., the mortgage status of a particular parcel) the intended individual, or is 'property status' intended as a general class covering all such statuses? The current proposal treats it as a class.

Should PropertyStatus be related to existing classes such as working:LegalRight or working:LegalObligation (e.g., ownership status entails a LegalRight)? If so, additional relations could be proposed.
proposal.rationale_summary: A 'property status' is most naturally classified as a BFO Quality (BFO_0000019): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer — typically a material entity (land parcel, building, chattel) or a legal person — and characterises that bearer at a given time. Examples include being owned, mortgaged, encumbered, held in trust, or abandoned. Qualities in BFO are intrinsic (in the sense of inhering in one bearer) and can change over time, which matches the way property statuses work legally. The alternative of BFO Role (BFO_0000023) is worth considering if the emphasis is on the externally conferred, socially recognised character of the status (e.g., 'owner' as a role borne by a person), but the status of the property itself — rather than the role of the person holding it — is better captured as a Quality. No existing working-ontology class covers this, so a new class WorkingPropertyStatus is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000019.
